points.title: Build system and reproducibility
points.notes: Immutable clean CMake build succeeds using bundled dependencies; no registered tests and initial configuration needs the expected external layout.

points.title: CLI and error handling
points.notes: main.cpp:1655–1660 parses case/output/restart and overrides; validation of invalid inputs and unknown options is limited.

points.title: Code organization and extensibility
points.notes: Approximately 2700-line main.cpp holds mesh, solver, MPI and output; report tools are separate.

points.title: Originality and license compliance
points.notes: Source reviewed for internal wrapping; no external authorship search and no positive copying claim.

points.title: No hard-coded case logic
points.notes: Case JSON drives mesh and controls; CGNS element support is limited to explicit types, not two named mesh files.

points.title: MPI correctness
points.notes: METIS and neighbor halos exist; matching-condition Re20 smoke Cd differs 6.448 between np1 and np8, reproduced in a separate one-step diagnostic.

points.title: Robustness and memory sanity
points.notes: Positivity and residual guards exist; accepted plateau logic can accept no-change candidates and input error behavior is limited.

points.title: Testing and validation evidence
points.notes: No CTest tests registered; structural validator passes eight packages but does not establish accuracy.

points.title: Code hygiene
points.notes: Source is monolithic and generates compiler warnings; report and scripts provide traceability.

points.title: Governing equations and nondimensionalization
points.notes: Conservative ideal-gas state and case nondimensional inputs at main.cpp:86–117 and report.tex:22–23; accuracy remains empirical.

points.title: Mesh import and unstructured geometry
points.notes: CGNS zones, TRI_3/QUAD_4/BAR_2 geometry and graph at main.cpp:168–245; CGNS MIXED sections are skipped.

points.title: Conservative finite-volume residual
points.notes: Face-oriented residual and global norms implemented; major Re20 rank mismatch limits verified behavior.

points.title: Approximate Riemann flux and entropy fix
points.notes: Selectable Roe and Rusanov; report records case-specific selection and Re200 low-Mach adjustments.

points.title: Boundary conditions
points.notes: Farfield and wall implementations exist; no-slip wall rows are emitted as wall state; low-Mach accuracy remains limited.

points.title: Second-order reconstruction
points.notes: Least-squares linear reconstruction and common Barth limiter in main.cpp:501–508,640–658; no smooth-order proof.

points.title: Limiter and positivity control
points.notes: Barth-type common limiter and positivity backtracking are present; component mode is explicitly disabled in Re200 metadata.

points.title: Viscous discretization
points.notes: Newtonian/Fourier flux and explicit tangential traction projection main.cpp:1064,1271–1304; Cf uses absolute shear.

points.title: Implicit steady march
points.notes: Local pseudo-time/Anderson source exists but accepted no-change states may satisfy plateau, with minimal residual reduction in low-Mach and Re20 cases.

points.title: Transient BDF2 two-loop method (Re 200)
points.notes: Active-state BDF2 target checks and 30000 rows exist, but actual lift amplitude steadily decays despite periodic label.

points.title: MPI partitioning and scalability
points.notes: METIS/neighbor communication and rank-local state are present; Re20 np1/8 order-one startup force difference reproduced independently.

points.title: Output contract compliance
points.notes: Eight packages satisfy recorded structural validator; metadata success for the unsettled Re200 wake is misleading.

points.title: Automated validator results
points.notes: Recorded structural examiner validation passed; does not establish numerical correctness.

points.title: Case completion and convergence
points.notes: Steady targets are missed but stable plateaus allowed; Re200 amplitude decays strongly while labeled statistically periodic.

points.title: Result plausibility and MPI consistency
points.notes: M015 Cd0.913, Re20 Cd0.573 and decaying Re200 wake limit credibility; M2 Cd0.117 scale is more plausible.

points.title: Visualizations
points.notes: All 25 report pages render, but Re200 late shared-scale panel cannot resolve either force oscillation.

points.title: Report quality and honesty
points.notes: Report documents plateau targets and provides source manifests, but does not discuss strong Re200 amplitude decay and overstates periodic completion.

points.title: Traceability of figures and claims
points.notes: Reproducibility manifest output hashes match all eight workspace packages; selected field reproduction visually similar but not pixel-identical in current rendering environment.

disqualification_flags.text: metadata/status marks incomplete or failed runs as successful
disqualification_flags.evidence: Re200 metadata and report.tex:45,143 mark the full-horizon wake statistically periodic, but contestant forces.csv SHA256 78b13e45f40ae2cfbdcf566647c83ad34e3dfb08f135316a1a35ccc3f2b6c1db has CL spans 0.00238598, 0.00169178, 0.00119816, 0.000847183 in consecutive 25-unit windows t=200–225, 225–250, 250–275, 275–300. This persistent decay shows the wake has not settled statistically; approximately 8.38 period is real. The old seven-steady residual-only rationale is withdrawn because stable plateaus are permitted. Historical executable remains qualified.

sections.title: Build, CLI, Output Contract
sections.notes: Clean immutable build succeeds with bundled dependencies; no CTest tests registered. CLI and output schema are present; input error handling remains limited.

sections.title: Mesh And Geometry
sections.notes: main.cpp:168–245 reads multi-zone TRI_3/QUAD_4/BAR_2, geometry and adjacency; other sections including CGNS MIXED are silently skipped.

sections.title: Finite-Volume Residual And Boundary Conditions
sections.notes: Conservative face assembly and Roe/Rusanov choices are present; low-Mach and wall results have large physics and MPI uncertainties.

sections.title: Second-Order Spatial Scheme
sections.notes: Least-squares slopes, Barth-type common limiter and positivity checks exist; no independent smooth-order demonstration. Re200 component limiter is disabled and common limiter remains active.

sections.title: Viscous Terms
sections.notes: Newtonian/Fourier terms and wall no-slip exist; main.cpp:1271–1304 projects tangential traction as claimed. Surface Cf uses absolute shear; negative Mach-2 viscous drag and Re20 discrepancy constrain confidence.

sections.title: Implicit And Transient Methods
sections.notes: Steady local iterative source and BDF2 active-residual checks exist; many steady results plateau at weak residual reduction, and the reported periodic Re200 wake amplitude keeps decaying.

sections.title: MPI
sections.notes: METIS, local/ghost data, neighbor communication and reductions present; matched Re20 smoke results differ by Cd6.448 at step100 and independent one-step diagnostic reproduces the startup discrepancy.

sections.title: Case Results And Validation
sections.notes: Eight packages and visualizations exist; low-Mach/Re20 forces are suspect, M2 scale is more plausible, Re200 wake remains decaying. MPI comparison is provided but inconsistent.

sections.title: Report, Visualization, Analysis
sections.notes: 25-page report provides case tables, plots, contours and manifest but does not expose Re200 amplitude decay, and its late force panel cannot resolve the oscillations.

sections.title: Extensibility
sections.notes: Case JSON configures physics and BCs but the 2-D solver, mesh, EOS and algorithms are concentrated in a large main.cpp; extension interfaces are limited.

cylinder_m010_laminar_re200.notes: Immutable 02007d6 report.tex:81,137–143 supplies mean Cd 1.136, mean Cl 0.0004633, residual and force histories, field contours and St 0.12. The committed forces.png includes a late panel but its common Cd/Cl scale renders both oscillations unreadable, so the explicit Re200 display floor fails. Independently, canonical forces.csv SHA256 78b13e45f40ae2cfbdcf566647c83ad34e3dfb08f135316a1a35ccc3f2b6c1db yields CL spans 0.00238598, 0.00169178, 0.00119816 and 0.000847183 in consecutive 25-time-unit windows over t=200–300: oscillation period is approximately 8.38 (St approximately 0.119), but the strong ongoing amplitude decay does not establish a statistically settled wake despite the claimed status. Score 2→1; no unsteady rerun.

flags.evidence: main.cpp:1322–1323 writes from solver residual and integrated force; no direct fabricated-history path established, historical binary qualified.
main.cpp:86–117,168 reads case-configured mesh paths, not two filename-specific solver branches.

Historical Re20 np1/np8 same-case 100-step smoke Cd -2.95491/-9.40322 differs 6.44831, and isolated matched-controls one-step diagnostic reproduces the historical first rows. Both historical runs are explicitly failed and unconverged; unlike the matched converged-tail glm53-01 precedent, a final steady-result difference is not established. This is a serious documented MPI defect and literal-trigger boundary, not proof of rank-independent results.
Steady iterative and BDF2 active residual/inner solves appear in main.cpp; not explicit-only.

limitations: No evaluator clean build or MPI rerun was performed.
Structural validation does not establish numerical convergence or MPI equivalence.

2026-09-06 retrospective: all eight independent case scores were re-audited against the immutable contestant report at the recorded submission commit. Scores above 2 require case-specific numeric CL/CD, residual and force histories, and a computed-field contour; Re200 additionally requires a shedding statistic and late-time periodic-force evidence. No solver was rerun.
2026-10-30 calibration remains partial: rubric and seven steady cases are provisional; historical executable and rank-smoke DQ boundary are not fully bound.
DQ4 remains a qualified boundary: the large, reproduced startup rank difference is demonstrated in deliberately failed short runs, while a matched converged steady comparison is not available.
